history.origins: Truf is a popular Indonesian trick-taking game with bidding, classified under the Exact Bidding group. The name is probably derived from the Dutch word troef (trump), reflecting historical Dutch influence in Indonesia. Players bid by placing a card from hand face down to propose trump suit and number of tricks; trumps are played face down and revealed only after each trick. The documented rules draw on information from Indonesian contributors Riza Purwo Nugroho, David Nugraha and Hamdanil Rasyid. The game is played in Indonesia and among Indonesian communities abroad (e.g. Singapore, California).
timeline: Traditional: Indonesian exact-bidding trick game; no specific century documented in primary sources.
history.cultural: Popular in Indonesia and in Indonesian diaspora communities. The Dutch-derived name (troef) and use of a standard international pack reflect colonial-era card-game diffusion.

setup.deck: 52 cards (4 players) or 39 (3 players, remove 1 black suit). 13 each.
setup.dealing: 13 cards each. Re-deal if hand is all number or all court cards.

rules.objective: Win exactly the number of tricks bid. Highest total score wins.
rules.gameplay: Bid by placing card face-down (rank = trick bid, court = 0). Highest bid selects trump (their card's suit). Play tricks. Follow suit. Trumps played face-down (hidden). Can't lead trump unless only trumps remain.
keyRules: Re-deal for all-number or all-court hands

strategy.basic: Bid conservatively. Use strong trumps to win exact count.
strategy.intermediate: Read opponent bids from card choice.
strategy.advanced: Track face-down trumps. Manage bid accuracy.
